primitives.name: Inference Routing
primitives.verbatim_quote: | | inference-routing | [`inference-routing/SKILL.md`](./inference-routing/SKILL.md) | MODEL_PRIMARY/MODEL_CHEAP routing and free-lane cost control.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'M_p': 'primary model', 'M_c': 'cheap model', 'C_p': 'cost of primary inference', 'C_c': 'cost of cheap inference'}
primitives.assumptions: Costs are known and fixed; models have distinct accuracy profiles; routing minimizes expected cost.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Routing fails if M_p or M_c becomes unavailable or misaligned with input distribution.

layer2.mapping: Routing operator selects between M_p and M_c based on cost-benefit trade-off defined by C_p and C_c.
layer2.telemetry: Cost per inference and model selection frequency

The autonomy kernel enables closed-loop execution without data invention, forming a deterministic state machine. Calibration pipeline applies Bayesian inference to settle predictions into calibrated allocations, using ECE and Kelly criteria. Inference routing optimizes computational cost by selecting between expensive and cheap models. These primitives form a layered architecture where lower layers provide foundational operations, while higher layers apply probabilistic reasoning and optimization. Dualities emerge in how each skill balances autonomy vs. constraint, efficiency vs. safety, and cost vs. performance. Failure modes are encoded explicitly to prevent cascading errors across the system.
